newsitem.title: USA: Clinton will speak at Arkansas friend's funeral.
newsitem.headline: Clinton will speak at Arkansas friend's funeral.

text.p: President Clinton flew to his home state Thursday to attend the funeral of Hilary Jones, a longtime friend and political supporter who backed him when he ran unsuccessfully for Congress at the age of 28.
Clinton told reporters travelling with him aboard Air Force One that Jones had been a beloved friend and he expected to speak at his funeral Friday morning.

"You know, once in a while in life you meet somebody and you know your life will never be the same again. That's how it was," the president said of his first encounter with Jones in 1974. "He was like a magnet. I just loved him."
Jones died Tuesday at the age of 70. He had been in ill health with pneumonia and suffered a heart attack.
Clinton spent the night in Harrison, located in the Ozark Mountains in northwest Arkansas, in preparation for attending the funeral at the Jasper First Baptist Church in Jasper, Arkansas, Friday.
After arriving in Harrison, Clinton paid a condolence visit to Jones' children, spending nearly two hours with them at the family home and staying long past midnight.

It was Clinton's second trip home within a month. The president travelled to Arkansas last month for the funeral of Henry Oren Grisham, a great-uncle whom Clinton called Uncle Buddy. He died at 92. Clinton's father, William Blythe, died three months before Clinton was born.
Virginia Laverty, Jones' daughter, said earlier this week her father loved Clinton and "treated him like a son."

"He was one of my closest personal friends," Clinton said of Jones, noting their friendship began in 1974, when Jones backed Clinton in his first election -- a long-shot campaign against incumbent Republican Representative John Paul Hammerschmidt.
Clinton lost but drew 48.2 percent of the vote, enough to get him noticed.
"It went way more than politics. I mean, I just loved him. He was a wise, good, decent, incredibly intelligent guy," a sombre Clinton told reporters as he flew to Arkansas.

Clinton, a native of Hope, Arkansas, said the Ozark region where Jones lived was isolated when he first visited. People were still making moonshine, the regional accent was very distinct, and there were caves filled with Civil War munitions.
Clinton said Jones "always liked the fact that I told somebody that he looked like a mountain man and he had an old Caterpillar cap on, but he had a 160 IQ."
"And that's basically what he was -- a brilliant man," he added.

Jones, a retired building contracter, was long active in Arkansas Democratic Party politics. When Clinton was governor, he named Jones to the Game and Fish Commission, a coveted appointment in Arkansas.
Clinton said he last saw Jones when the contracter stayed at the White House several years ago. But said the two kept in touch and the family immediately called him from the hospital when Jones died.

Remembering his departure from Arkansas after winning the presidency in 1992, Clinton said he told his staff: "There are just a few people that if anything should happen to them while I'm president, whatever I'm doing, I've got to go home.
